question:
A company must migrate 20 TB of data from a data center to the AWS Cloud within 30 days. The company’s network bandwidth is limited to 15
Mbps and cannot exceed 70% utilization.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Use AWS Snowball.
incorrectAnswers: Use AWS DataSync.
Use a secure VPN connection.
Use Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration.
explanation:
20 TB over 10.5 Mbps (70% of 15 Mbps) would take roughly 176 days, so online options (DataSync, VPN, Transfer Acceleration) cannot meet 30 days. Note: AWS Snowball Edge is no longer available to new customers; AWS now recommends AWS Data Transfer Terminal for physical transfers.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/snowball/latest/developer-guide/whatisedge.html

factChecks.explanation: For the exam scenario, the key holds: 20 TB at 10.5 Mbps takes about 176 days online, so an offline device is needed. A company’s application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto
Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. On the first day of every month at midnight, the application becomes much slower when the
month-end financial calculation batch runs. This causes the CPU utilization of the EC2 instances to immediately peak to 100%, which disrupts the
application.
What should a solutions architect recommend to ensure the application is able to handle the workload and avoid downtime?
correctAnswer: Configure an EC2 Auto Scaling scheduled scaling policy based on the monthly schedule.
incorrectAnswers: Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the ALB.
Configure an EC2 Auto Scaling simple scaling policy based on CPU utilization.
Configure Amazon ElastiCache to remove some of the workload from the EC2 instances.
explanation:
A scheduled action can raise desired capacity shortly before midnight on the first of the month so instances are ready when the batch starts. Reactive CPU-based scaling lags behind the instant spike, and CloudFront or ElastiCache do not offload a compute-heavy batch job.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-scheduled-scaling.html

factChecks.explanation: The load is predictable (first of the month at midnight) and CPU spikes immediately, so reactive scaling is too slow. Scheduled scaling adds capacity ahead of the batch. CloudFront caching does not help a CPU-bound batch calculation.

correctAnswer: Enable Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) fast snapshot restore on a snapshot. Provision an AMI by using the snapshot. Replace the AMI in the Auto Scaling group with the new AMI.
incorrectAnswers: Use the aws ec2 register-image command to create an AMI from a snapshot. Use AWS Step Functions to replace the AMI in the Auto Scaling group.

A company has deployed a web application on AWS. The company hosts the backend database on Amazon RDS for MySQL with a primary DB
instance and five read replicas to support scaling needs. The read replicas must lag no more than 1 second behind the primary DB instance. The
database routinely runs scheduled stored procedures.
As traffic on the website increases, the replicas experience additional lag during periods of peak load. A solutions architect must reduce the
replication lag as much as possible. The solutions architect must minimize changes to the application code and must minimize ongoing
operational overhead.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora MySQL. Replace the read replicas with Aurora Replicas, and configure Aurora Auto Scaling. Replace the stored procedures with Aurora MySQL native functions.
incorrectAnswers: Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster in front of the database. Modify the application to check the cache before the application queries the database. Replace the stored procedures with AWS Lambda functions.
Migrate the database to a MySQL database that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. Choose large, compute optimized EC2 instances for all replica nodes. Maintain the stored procedures on the EC2 instances.

Migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB. Provision a large number of read capacity units (RCUs) to support the required throughput, and configure on-demand capacity scaling. Replace the stored procedures with DynamoDB streams.
explanation:
Aurora Replicas share the cluster storage volume so replica lag is typically milliseconds, and Aurora Auto Scaling adds replicas with minimal operations. ElastiCache needs code changes and EC2-hosted MySQL adds operational burden.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Overview.StorageReliability.html

factChecks.explanation: Key (Aurora MySQL with Aurora Replicas and auto scaling) is correct (replica lag usually under 100 ms); explanation is EC2 Auto Scaling text. Ligatures.

A solutions architect must create a disaster recovery (DR) plan for a high-volume software as a service (SaaS) platform. All data for the platform
is stored in an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster.
The DR plan must replicate data to a secondary AWS Region.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
correctAnswer: Set up an Aurora global database for the DB cluster. When setup is complete, remove the DB instance from the secondary Region.
incorrectAnswers: Use MySQL binary log replication to an Aurora cluster in the secondary Region. Provision one DB instance for the Aurora cluster in the secondary Region.
Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to continuously replicate data to an Aurora cluster in the secondary Region. Remove the DB instance from the secondary Region.
Set up an Aurora global database for the DB cluster. Specify a minimum of one DB instance in the secondary Region.
explanation:
An Aurora global database replicates at the storage layer, and a headless secondary cluster (no DB instance) avoids instance charges until failover. DMS cannot replicate to a cluster with no instance, and binlog or an extra instance adds cost.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-global-database-getting-started.html

factChecks.explanation: Aurora Global Database supports a headless secondary cluster (no DB instance), so storage-level replication continues at lowest cost; binlog replication with a provisioned instance costs more and is more work.

QuickSight by joining the data in the data lake with operational data that is stored in an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. The company wants to
enforce column-level authorization so that the company’s marketing team can access only a subset of columns in the database.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
correctAnswer: Use a Lake Formation blueprint to ingest the data from the database to the S3 data lake. Use Lake Formation to enforce column-level access control for the QuickSight users. Use Amazon Athena as the data source in QuickSight.
incorrectAnswers: Use Amazon EMR to ingest the data directly from the database to the QuickSight SPICE engine. Include only the required columns.

Use AWS Glue Studio to ingest the data from the database to the S3 data lake. Attach an IAM policy to the QuickSight users to enforce column-level access control. Use Amazon S3 as the data source in QuickSight.

explanation:
Lake Formation centrally governs the lake with column-level permissions enforced for Athena queries, and can import database data itself, giving the least operational overhead. IAM policies or S3 bucket policies cannot enforce column-level access, and EMR adds cluster management and bypasses Lake Formation.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/what-is-lake-formation.html

factChecks.explanation: Keyed EMR-to-SPICE option bypasses Lake Formation governance and is high overhead. question:
A transaction processing company has weekly scripted batch jobs that run on Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances are in an Auto Scaling
group. The number of transactions can vary, but the baseline CPU utilization that is noted on each run is at least 60%. The company needs to
provision the capacity 30 minutes before the jobs run.
Currently, engineers complete this task by manually modifying the Auto Scaling group parameters. The company does not have the resources to
analyze the required capacity trends for the Auto Scaling group counts. The company needs an automated way to modify the Auto Scaling group’s
desired capacity.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
correctAnswer: Create a predictive scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group. Configure the policy to scale based on forecast. Set the scaling metric to CPU utilization. Set the target value for the metric to 60%. In the policy, set the instances to pre-launch 30 minutes before the jobs run.
incorrectAnswers: Create a dynamic scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group. Configure the policy to scale based on the CPU utilization metric. Set the target value for the metric to 60%.

Create a scheduled scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group. Set the appropriate desired capacity, minimum capacity, and maximum capacity. Set the recurrence to weekly. Set the start time to 30 minutes before the batch jobs run.

Create an Amazon EventBridge event to invoke an AWS Lambda function when the CPU utilization metric value for the Auto Scaling group reaches 60%. Configure the Lambda function to increase the Auto Scaling group's desired capacity and maximum capacity by 20%.
explanation:
Predictive scaling forecasts recurring load such as weekly batch jobs and launches instances ahead of time (pre-launch), without the team analyzing capacity trends. Dynamic scaling only reacts after load arrives.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-predictive-scaling.html

factChecks.explanation: Dynamic scaling is reactive and would not provision 30 minutes ahead. The team cannot analyze trends, which points to predictive scaling (forecast + pre-launch time). Scheduled scaling is defensible but requires known capacity numbers; predictive scaling is the best-practice match.

correctAnswer: Migrate the MySQL database to an Amazon Aurora global database. Host the primary DB cluster in the primary Region. Host the secondary DB cluster in the DR Region.
incorrectAnswers: Migrate the MySQL database to multiple EC2 instances. Configure a standby EC2 instance in the DR Region. Turn on replication.

Store the scheduled backup of the MySQL database in an Amazon S3 bucket that is configured for S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR). Use the data backup to restore the database in the DR Region.
explanation:
Aurora global database provides fully managed, storage-based cross-Region replication with low RPO/RTO. Self-managed replication on EC2 requires you to operate and patch everything, RDS Multi-AZ is within one Region, and restoring from CRR backups has the longest recovery time.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-global-database.html

factChecks.explanation: Self-managed MySQL replication across Regions on EC2 is the highest operational overhead. Aurora global database (managed cross-Region replication, typically <1s latency, failover in about a minute) is the least overhead multi-Region DR option.

A company stores confidential data in an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database in the ap-southeast-3 Region. The database is encrypted with an
AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. The company was recently acquired and must securely share a backup of the
database with the acquiring company’s AWS account in ap-southeast-3.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Create a database snapshot. Add the acquiring company's AWS account to the KMS key policy. Share the snapshot with the acquiring company's AWS account.
incorrectAnswers: Create a database snapshot. Copy the snapshot to a new unencrypted snapshot. Share the new snapshot with the acquiring company's AWS account.
Create a database snapshot that uses a different AWS managed KMS key. Add the acquiring company's AWS account to the KMS key alias. Share the snapshot with the acquiring company's AWS account.
Create a database snapshot. Download the database snapshot. Upload the database snapshot to an Amazon S3 bucket. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the acquiring company's AWS account.
explanation:

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-share-snapshot.html

factChecks.explanation: Encrypted snapshots cannot be made unencrypted (copies stay encrypted). Correct: share the snapshot encrypted with the customer managed key and add the acquirer to the KMS key policy.

communicate between VPCs. The applications also must be able to consistently send hundreds of gigabytes of data each day to a latency-
sensitive application that runs in a single on-premises data center.
A solutions architect needs to design a network connectivity solution that maximizes cost-effectiveness.
Which solution meets these requirements?
correctAnswer: Set up one AWS Direct Connect connection from the data center to AWS. Create a transit gateway, and attach each VPC to the transit gateway. Establish connectivity between the Direct Connect connection and the transit gateway.
incorrectAnswers: Configure three AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections from the data center to AWS. Establish connectivity by configuring one VPN connection for each VPC.
Launch a third-party virtual network appliance in each VPC. Establish an IPsec VPN tunnel between the data center and each virtual appliance.
Set up three AWS Direct Connect connections from the data center to a Direct Connect gateway in us-east-1. Establish connectivity by configuring each VPC to use one of the Direct Connect connections.
explanation:
A single Direct Connect link provides consistent low-latency bandwidth, and a transit gateway interconnects the three VPCs and the on-premises network. Internet VPNs are inconsistent, and three separate Direct Connect links cost more.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/aws-vpc-connectivity-options/aws-direct-connect-aws-transit-gateway.html

factChecks.explanation: Site-to-Site VPN cannot deliver consistent, latency-sensitive hundreds of GB/day (internet-based, 1.25 Gbps/tunnel). Direct Connect + transit gateway connects all three VPCs over one dedicated link cost-effectively.

A company hosts a frontend application that uses an Amazon API Gateway API backend that is integrated with AWS Lambda. When the API
receives requests, the Lambda function loads many libraries. Then the Lambda function connects to an Amazon RDS database, processes the
data, and returns the data to the frontend application. The company wants to ensure that response latency is as low as possible for all its users
with the fewest number of changes to the company's operations.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Configure provisioned concurrency for the Lambda function that handles the requests.
incorrectAnswers: Establish a connection between the frontend application and the database to make queries faster by bypassing the API.
Cache the results of the queries in Amazon S3 for faster retrieval of similar datasets.
Increase the size of the database to increase the number of connections Lambda can establish at one time.
explanation:
Provisioned concurrency keeps pre-initialized execution environments (libraries already loaded) ready, removing cold-start latency with no application changes. Exposing the database directly to the frontend is insecure, and caching in S3 or a larger database do not remove initialization time.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/provisioned-concurrency.html

factChecks.explanation: Bypassing the API to connect the frontend directly to RDS is insecure and not an answer. Latency from loading libraries (cold start) is addressed by provisioned concurrency.

DB instances. The company wants a solution that automatically starts and stops the EC2 instances and DB instances outside of business hours.
The solution must minimize cost and infrastructure maintenance.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Create an AWS Lambda function that will start and stop the EC2 instances and DB instances. Configure Amazon EventBridge to invoke the Lambda function on a schedule.
incorrectAnswers: Scale the EC2 instances by using elastic resize. Scale the DB instances to zero outside of business hours.
Explore AWS Marketplace for partner solutions that will automatically start and stop the EC2 instances and DB instances on a schedule.
Launch another EC2 instance. Configure a crontab schedule to run shell scripts that will start and stop the existing EC2 instances and DB instances on a schedule.
explanation:
A scheduled Lambda function can stop and start EC2 and RDS instances with no servers to maintain and no extra cost. Elastic resize and scaling to zero do not apply to EC2 and RDS, and a cron EC2 instance or partner product adds cost and upkeep.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/solutions/latest/instance-scheduler-on-aws/solution-overview.html

factChecks.explanation: Keyed answer is invalid: 'elastic resize' is a Redshift feature and RDS instances cannot scale to zero. Lambda plus EventBridge schedule is the managed start/stop approach (also packaged as Instance Scheduler on AWS).

two private subnets for MySQL. The web servers use only HTTPS. The solutions architect has already created a security group for the load
balancer allowing port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. Company policy requires that each resource has the least access required to still be able to perform its
tasks.
Which additional configuration strategy should the solutions architect use to meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Create a security group for the web servers and allow port 443 from the load balancer. Create a security group for the MySQL servers and allow port 3306 from the web servers security group.
incorrectAnswers: Create a network ACL for the web servers and allow port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. Create a network ACL for the MySQL servers and allow port 3306 from the web servers security group.

question:
An IAM user made several configuration changes to AWS resources in their company's account during a production deployment last week. A
solutions architect learned that a couple of security group rules are not configured as desired. The solutions architect wants to confirm which IAM
user was responsible for making changes.
Which service should the solutions architect use to find the desired information?
correctAnswer: AWS CloudTrail
incorrectAnswers: Amazon GuardDuty
Amazon Inspector
AWS Config
explanation:

question:
A company has implemented a self-managed DNS service on AWS. The solution consists of the following:
• Amazon EC2 instances in different AWS Regions
• Endpoints of a standard accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator
The company wants to protect the solution against DDoS attacks.
What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement?
correctAnswer: Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced. Add the accelerator as a resource to protect.
incorrectAnswers: Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced. Add the EC2 instances as resources to protect.
Create an AWS WAF web ACL that includes a rate-based rule. Associate the web ACL with the accelerator.
Create an AWS WAF web ACL that includes a rate-based rule. Associate the web ACL with the EC2 instances.
explanation:
AWS Shield Advanced can protect Global Accelerator standard accelerators as a protected resource. Because traffic enters through the accelerator, protecting the accelerator (not the EC2 endpoints) is the correct choice. question:
An ecommerce company needs to run a scheduled daily job to aggregate and filter sales records for analytics. The company stores the sales
records in an Amazon S3 bucket. Each object can be up to 10 GB in size. Based on the number of sales events, the job can take up to an hour to

A solutions architect needs to minimize the amount of operational effort that is needed for the job to run.
Which solution meets these requirements?
correctAnswer: Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with an AWS Fargate launch type. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event that launches an ECS task on the cluster to run the job.
incorrectAnswers: Create an AWS Lambda function that has an Amazon EventBridge notification. Schedule the EventBridge event to run once a day.

Create an AWS Lambda function. Create an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API, and integrate the API with the function. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event that calls the API and invokes the function.

Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with an Amazon EC2 launch type and an Auto Scaling group with at least one EC2 instance. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event that launches an ECS task on the cluster to run the job.

Fargate tasks can run longer than an hour without servers to manage and EventBridge schedules them daily. Lambda is limited to a 15-minute timeout, and the EC2 launch type requires managing instances.

question:

ability to retrieve current stock prices. The company’s security team has noticed an increase in the number of API requests. The security team is

Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
correctAnswer: Create a Regional AWS WAF web ACL with a rate-based rule. Associate the web ACL with the API Gateway stage.
incorrectAnswers: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the API Gateway Regional API endpoint with a maximum TTL of 24 hours.
Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics to monitor the Count metric and alert the security team when the predefined rate is reached.

explanation:
A rate-based rule in a Regional AWS WAF web ACL associated with the API Gateway stage blocks IPs that exceed a request rate, with no custom code. Monitoring only alerts, and Lambda@Edge needs custom code.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-rule-statement-type-rate-based.html

factChecks.explanation: Protecting from HTTP floods with least overhead: AWS WAF rate-based rule on the API Gateway stage. CloudFront caching alone is not flood protection for dynamic requests.

question:
A meteorological startup company has a custom web application to sell weather data to its users online. The company uses Amazon DynamoDB
to store its data and wants to build a new service that sends an alert to the managers of four internal teams every time a new weather event is
recorded. The company does not want this new service to affect the performance of the current application.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?
correctAnswer: Enable Amazon DynamoDB Streams on the table. Use triggers to write to a single Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to which the teams can subscribe.
incorrectAnswers: Use DynamoDB transactions to write new event data to the table. Configure the transactions to notify internal teams.
Have the current application publish a message to four Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topics. Have each team subscribe to one topic.

Add a custom attribute to each record to flag new items. Write a cron job that scans the table every minute for items that are new and notifies an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue to which the teams can subscribe.
explanation:
DynamoDB Streams captures item changes asynchronously with no performance impact on the table, and a Lambda trigger can publish to one SNS topic that all four teams subscribe to. Transactions provide ACID writes, not notifications, and changing the app or scanning the table adds load/overhead.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Streams.html

factChecks.explanation: DynamoDB transactions cannot send notifications. DynamoDB Streams (asynchronous, no table performance impact) triggering Lambda to publish to an SNS topic is the standard least-overhead design.

question:

question:
A developer has an application that uses an AWS Lambda function to upload files to Amazon S3 and needs the required permissions to perform
the task. The developer already has an IAM user with valid IAM credentials required for Amazon S3.
What should a solutions architect do to grant the permissions?
correctAnswer: Create an IAM execution role with the required permissions and attach the IAM role to the Lambda function.
incorrectAnswers: Add required IAM permissions in the resource policy of the Lambda function.
Create a signed request using the existing IAM credentials in the Lambda function.
Create a new IAM user and use the existing IAM credentials in the Lambda function.
explanation:
A Lambda execution role grants the function permission to call AWS services such as S3 using temporary credentials. A function resource policy controls who can invoke the function, and embedding long-term credentials is insecure.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-intro-execution-role.html

factChecks.explanation: Lambda gets S3 permissions through an IAM execution role, not a resource policy (which controls who may invoke the function) and not embedded user credentials.

question:
A company has deployed a serverless application that invokes an AWS Lambda function when new documents are uploaded to an Amazon S3
bucket. The application uses the Lambda function to process the documents. After a recent marketing campaign, the company noticed that the
application did not process many of the documents.
What should a solutions architect do to improve the architecture of this application?
correctAnswer: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Send the requests to the queue. Configure the queue as an event source for Lambda.
incorrectAnswers: Set the Lambda function's runtime timeout value to 15 minutes.
Configure an S3 bucket replication policy. Stage the documents in the S3 bucket for later processing.
Deploy an additional Lambda function. Load balance the processing of the documents across the two Lambda functions.
explanation:
An SQS queue buffers the upload events and Lambda polls it, retrying failed messages so none are lost during bursts. Raising the timeout, replication or a second function does not stop dropped events.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sqs.html

factChecks.explanation: Documents unprocessed after a spike: decouple with SQS as Lambda event source so events are buffered and retried; a 15-minute timeout does not address bursts. Explanation unrelated.

question:

explanation:

question:

Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with the Fargate launch type. Create an ECS service on the cluster. Set the ECS service as the target for the NLB. Process the data in Amazon ECS.
incorrectAnswers: Configure an Amazon Route 53 failover routing policy. Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in each of the two Regions. Configure the NLB to invoke an AWS Lambda function to process the data.

Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with the Fargate launch type. Create an ECS service on the cluster. Set the ECS service as the target for the ALB. explanation:
Global Accelerator routes UDP over the AWS backbone and fails over between Regions in seconds without DNS caching delays; NLB supports UDP; ALB does not.

question:

share hosted in the user's on-premises network-attached storage (NAS). The solutions architect has proposed migrating the IIS web servers to

correctAnswer: Migrate the file share to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server.
incorrectAnswers: Migrate the file share to Amazon RDS.

question:

Encryption is turned on when an EBS volume is created (or via encryption by default), which encrypts data at rest. IAM roles, instance tags and KMS key policies do not enforce volume encryption.

question:

question:

weeks. Other models could receive batches of thousands of requests at a time.
Which design should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Direct the requests from the API into an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Deploy the models as Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) services that read from the queue. question:
